covers.quote: Break telephone numbers into shorter blocks of digits or ‘chunks’.
For landline telephone numbers, write the 2-digit area code followed by a non-breaking space. Then write the rest of the number in 2 chunks of 4 digits.
Write mobile telephone numbers in 1 chunk of 4 digits and then 2 chunks of 3 digits.
write the telephone number in 2 chunks of 4 digits.
write the telephone number in 3 chunks of 3 digits.

rules.quote: Use ‘chunks’ of digits to help people read telephone numbers
rules.violation_condition: A displayed telephone number is written as one undivided string of digits, or an Australian landline or mobile number has digit-group boundaries that differ from the specified pattern for its number type and national or international format.
when: Applies to displayed telephone numbers, not the space-free destination in a tel: URL.
Australian national-format landlines have a 2-digit area-code group followed by 2 groups of 4 digits.
Australian national-format mobiles have groups of 4, 3 and 3 digits.
International-format Australian landlines have the country code and area code followed by 2 groups of 4 digits.
International-format Australian mobiles have 3 groups of 3 digits after the country code.
Other telephone-number categories must still be chunked, but this rule does not impose a universal 10-digit length or infer additional mandatory group sizes from examples.
rules.why: G-2 combines number-type and format cases into one digit-grouping check; G-4 absorbs the general restatement. Separator characters and numbering prefixes are separate properties.

when: Applies between chunks of a displayed telephone number, not inside its tel: URL.
Use a non-breaking space, U+00A0, in the general case.
For print, use a narrow no-break space, U+202F.

rules.why: G-2 treats print as a condition changing the required separator, not a second spacing rule; G-4 absorbs repeated instructions and the HTML representation.

rules.quote: Use international format for content that will be used outside Australia.

when: Australian telephone numbers in content intended for use within Australia use national format.
Australian telephone numbers in content intended for use outside Australia use international format.

rules.quote: Make telephone numbers accessible through ‘click-to-call’ functionality
rules.violation_condition: A telephone number in HTML content lacks a corresponding click-to-call link using a tel: URL.
when: Applies to telephone numbers in HTML content that supports links, not to printed text.
Support click-to-call explicitly with HTML rather than relying on a device to recognise the displayed number automatically.
The link destination uses tel: followed by the telephone number.
Spaces and international prefixes in the link destination have their own checks.
rules.why: G-4 combines the accessibility instruction and its explicit tel: implementation so a missing telephone link produces one finding.

rules.violation_condition: The telephone-number component of a tel: URL contains spaces between its digits.
when: Applies to the destination telephone number in a click-to-call URL.
Does not prohibit the required non-breaking spaces in the displayed link text.
rules.why: The grain test separates spaces inside an existing tel: destination from the absence of a click-to-call link.

rules.quote: Include the international dialling prefix if appropriate.
rules.specification: The page does not define when an international prefix is appropriate for a click-to-call destination. Do not treat every national-format destination as violating: the page supplies both national and international tel: examples.
rules.violation_condition: A click-to-call destination omits an international dialling prefix in a context where that prefix is appropriate.
when: Applies to click-to-call destinations on webpages.
Webpages can be accessed internationally, but the instruction remains conditional on appropriateness.
rules.why: G-2 retains the appropriateness condition; E-4 prevents replacing that condition with an invented requirement that every web telephone link be international.

covers.quote: Always display the telephone number as digits. Don’t use ‘phone words’. Use the relevant 13 or 1300 number instead.

rules.violation_condition: A telephone number is displayed using letters or a digit-word combination that readers must convert to digits.
when: Display the telephone number as digits.
When replacing a phone word for a 13 or 1300 service, display its corresponding numeric telephone number.
rules.why: G-4 combines the prohibition, its positive digit-only restatement and the numeric replacement instruction into one finding; “Always” makes the digit-only requirement categorical.
